title: The Influence of Light Colour Temperatures on Interior Design Student Performance in Classroom Studies
research_question: How do lighting conditions (light colour temperatures) impact interior design students' perceived spatial quality, comfort, collaboration, motivation, distraction, and fatigue in a classroom studio?

participants.description: Interior design students at Irbid University College, Jordan. Majority female (60.5%), aged 18-24 years (86.3%), primarily first-year students (65.3%).
participants.recruitment: Students studying interior design at Irbid University College were selected as the target population.

stimuli_or_exposures.description: A design studio (80 m²) at Irbid University College, Jordan, where students experienced and reported on conditions under 'Daylight colour temperature', 'High colour temperature', and 'Low colour temperature'. A 'High Light scenario' was also presented (Figure 1a).

measures.instrument: Survey questionnaire (rating scales for overall spaciousness, amount of natural light, brightness level)
Survey questionnaire (rating scales for comfort, ease of collaboration, distraction by external factors)
Survey questionnaire (rating scales for motivation to work, efficiency completing tasks, feeling fatigued/tired)
Survey questionnaire (gender, age, current year of study, frequency of attending design studios per week)

mechanisms: High light colour temperatures, including daylight, can make students more focused and attentive, leading to greater personal productivity.
Warm white and other low-light colour temperatures may produce a comfortable and personal ambience, encouraging cooperation and interpersonal communication.
Lighting conditions significantly affect perceived comfort, collaboration, motivation, distraction, and fatigue.
Proper use of correlated colour temperature can boost motivation, enhance health, and support cognitive functions.
Psychologically and visually comfortable conditions, facilitated by light quantity and quality, affirm well-being and heighten desire to work harder and achieve better results.
moderators: Nature of the task carried out in the design studio
implementation_implications: Educators and designers should consider lighting conditions when creating conducive and comfortable learning environments.
Educational spaces should be designed with lighting systems that provide abundant natural light, high colour temperatures, and appropriate brightness levels.
Creating a comfortable and efficient atmosphere can positively influence students' motivation, teamwork, and productivity.
Consider diverse student preferences and seek feedback to ensure lighting meets their needs.
Educational institutions can create optimal lighting environments to promote student well-being, engagement, and academic success.

limitations: The sample size was limited to 124 interior design students from a specific university, which may limit the generalizability of the findings to a larger population.
The study relied on self-reported data, which could be subject to biases or inaccuracies.
The study focused only on the impact of light colour temperatures and did not consider other potential factors that could influence students' experiences in design studios.

mechanism_chain.description: Light colour temperature influences the perceived spaciousness of a classroom studio.
